newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries drop off Magellan's top 10 list.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries drop off Magellan's top 10 list.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries fell from the top ten holdings list on Fidelity Investments's Magellan Fund as of December 31, according to the latest issue of Fidelity's monthly mutual fund guide.
The top holdings in Magellan at December 31 were Intel Corp, General Electric Co, and Philip Morris Cos Inc, followed by International Business Machines Corp, and Chrysler Corp.
At November 30, the top holding in Magellan was U.S. Treasury notes due in 2005, followed by Intel, GE, Chrysler and IBM.

Stocks in Magellan's asset allocation at December 31 increased to 89.6 percent from 88.5 percent at November 30. Bonds fell to 3.8 percent from 7.9 percent, while cash rose to 6.6 percent from 3.6 percent, according to the stock guide.
Energy remained the top sector at 14.5 percent at December 31 versus 13.9 percent at November 30.

Technology stocks remained the second largest sector at 13.7 percent versus 13.6 percent at November 30, while consumer durables stayed in third place at 9.5 percent at December 31, off from 10.1 percent at November 30.
Magellan's net assets rose to $55.15 billion at January 31, compared to $53.99 billion at December 31.
